answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the zephyr identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 54 runs and collects one. Because the horizon index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the meadow audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 54 answers need 54 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
